approved: Aviation Legislation Amendment (Liability and Insurance) Bill 2020
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
The bill would update Australia's civil aviation liability and insurance framework.
It would increase liability caps and minimum insurance amounts for passenger death or injury, and expand regulation-making powers to allow future adjustments by regulation.
The liability limit for domestic passenger death or injury would be raised from $725,000 to $925,000, and the minimum insurance amount for domestic travel would increase from $725,000 to $925,000.
Increase liability limits for passenger death or injury, baggage loss, and international flights to reflect amounts set in 2019 regulations.
Increase the minimum amount of insurance carriers must purchase for domestic and international travel.
Expand regulation-making powers to allow the government to increase liability caps and insurance amounts by regulation, including possible automatic indexation.
Allow the Secretary to make determinations about acceptable insurance exclusions, enabling mandatory war risk insurance.
Clarify that servants and agents of air carriers can rely on the same liability conditions and limits as carriers.
Update the Air Accidents (Commonwealth Government Liability) Act 1963 to incorporate future liability cap increases whether made by the principal Act or regulation.
Civil aviation carriers, passengers, servants and agents of air carriers, and the Commonwealth government.

The Aviation Legislation Amendment (Liability and Insurance) Bill 2020 increases mandatory insurance requirements for air carriers to match liability caps raised under 2019 regulations, and expands regulation-making powers to allow future increases, potentially via automatic indexation, and to extend required insurance to risks such as war. It also clarifies that carriers and their servants and agents share the same scope of liability, with further stakeholder consultation planned on additional technical amendments.

The bill raises liability caps for domestic passenger death or injury to $725,000 and increases insurance requirements, but the speaker criticised the government’s failure to provide a sector-wide support plan for aviation during COVID-19, citing the loss of thousands of jobs at Virgin, Qantas, and dnata, and moved a second reading amendment calling for a recovery plan.

The speaker argued that the Aviation Legislation Amendment (Liability and Insurance) Bill 2020 increases liability caps for domestic air carriers: from $725,000 to $995,000 for passenger death or injury, from $900 to $3,000 for registered baggage, and from $90 to $300 for non-registered baggage, with a mechanism to adjust these amounts by regulation and potentially include war risks. The government plans to release a five-year aviation plan in 2021.

The Aviation Legislation Amendment (Liability and Insurance) Bill 2020 was supported for updating liability caps and insurance requirements, while the speaker criticised the Morrison government for failing to protect aviation workers during COVID-19—specifically, allowing Qantas to sack 2,500 ground staff despite receiving nearly $800 million in JobKeeper—and called for an equity injection into Virgin and a long-term aviation plan.

The Aviation Legislation Amendment (Liability and Insurance) Bill 2020 aims to protect the rights of the Australian flying public and provide greater certainty for air carriers. The amendments will further protect the rights and entitlements of the public and carriers involved in or affected by air accidents.
